capabilityMap.about: What Iris can judge, cell by cell: ten evaluation questions against six subjects. `has` means at least one shipped, measured thing answers the question for that subject; `partial` means something answers it with a stated limit; `gap` means nothing does yet; `n/a` means the question does not apply to the subject. Every `has` or `partial` cell names its evidence — a rule, a tool, a resource, a route, a proof row or a judge template — and each name resolves to something registered in this release (tests/capability-map-contract.test.ts). `needs` lists the inputs a call must carry for the cell's rules to judge; without them those rules skip and the verdict's `coverage` says so.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Deterministic detectors for leaked personal data and credentials, injection-shaped output and deployment-prohibited words, each fire naming the pattern and the span; precision and recall are published per rule at https://iris-eval.com/proof, not yet per entity.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The safety detectors read the output; supplying the input changes nothing for them, so the single-output answer carries over. A keyed judge template for harm potential exists and is unmeasured.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Tool outputs are never scanned for injected directives, and no rule relates a directive in a tool result to a later action.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs of one input exists, so nothing can say safe on nine of ten runs.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over a time window are served to the dashboard, with no interval and no cohort key.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The three safety detectors are measured on a labelled corpus with 95% intervals, and every fire carries its positive predictive value at the stated prior; robustness to obfuscated text is not yet measured.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Without an input only two context-free fabrication signals run, and the result says so; the grounded signals need the material the agent was given.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: A deterministic detector with context-grounded contradiction signals, measured with intervals; keyed judge templates for accuracy, correctness against a reference and faithfulness to sources, plus a citation verifier, cover what patterns cannot — on a key the user supplies.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Tool outputs are not yet read as grounding material, so a claim that contradicts what the agent itself read goes unjudged.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Consistency of claims across repeated runs of one input is not evaluated.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: No cohort or baseline; only per-rule failure rates over time.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The fabrication detector is measured on its corpus; the judge templates are unmeasured until a user-supplied key runs the judge harness, and the page says pending until then.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Form is measured — length, sentence count, non-empty, and stub or placeholder markers — not whether the ask was answered.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: Coverage of an expected answer's terms is measured when one is supplied; nothing yet reads the structure of the ask to see which parts were answered.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: No completeness rule reads the trajectory to see which parts of the ask were acted on.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over time only.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The completeness rules are measured as conformance to their stated formula, and each result says so in its uncertainty basis rather than presenting the number as a detection rate.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Both relevance rules skip without the input; on a single output the question is unanswerable and the verdict's coverage says so.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: Lexical: the share of the input's content terms the output carries, and continuity of topic across sentences, with a stated tokenizer and thresholds; a keyed helpfulness judge template exists and is unmeasured.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Nothing relates the trajectory to the ask, so a wrong tool for the question goes unjudged on every path.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over time only.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The relevance rules are measured as conformance to their lexical formula; the proof does not yet include cases where the formula and a reader would disagree.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Task completion cannot be judged from the output alone, and no rule attempts it.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: No rule reads the structure of the ask, so an answer that addresses one part of three and drops the rest reads as complete.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: No rule judges whether the trajectory completed the task; the real-transcript acceptance record names this as open.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs; completes the task seven of ten runs is not expressible.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: No cohort or baseline.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: No completion evaluator exists to measure.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Acting well is a property of the trajectory, not of a single output.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: As for a single output.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Two deterministic trajectory rules — a failed tool call the output never acknowledges, and a repeated call with the same input — measured with intervals; tool choice and argument validity have no evaluator yet.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts for the two trajectory rules over time only.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Both trajectory rules are measured with intervals on their corpus families, and each fire carries its positive predictive value.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Trace cost and token usage are captured and judged by the cost bundle, and the evaluator's own spend — the judge's tokens and cost — is stored on the evaluation.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: A cost ceiling and a token ratio are judged from the trace totals; the ratio measures verbosity, not efficiency, and says so.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Cost is judged on the trace total; per-call latency is recorded, per-call tokens and cost are not yet.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs, and no rule reads an agent's own cost distribution.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Aggregate cost over a time window is served to the dashboard; the cost-spike classifier uses a fixed threshold rather than the agent's own distribution.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The cost rules are measured as conformance to their formula, and the evaluator's own spend is stored per evaluation.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Better or worse than before needs at least two things to compare.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: As for a single output.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: No comparison of trajectories across runs.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Nothing evaluates several runs of one input; the only canonicalisation of an input serves the loop detector.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Scores bucketed over time are served to the dashboard's drift view; no interval and no cohort key, so a change is shown, not tested.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Nothing measures whether a rule change made the evaluator better or worse beyond the proof-number diff in CI.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Every fired detection carries typed evidence — offsets into the raw output, never a paraphrase — and a message naming the pattern; the stored evaluation reads back the same way.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The grounded signals name the contradiction they found; measurements carry their value, unit and the threshold they were held to and where it came from.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A silent tool failure names the failed call by index, why it failed and what the output claimed instead; a loop names every repeated call and the threshold.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: No grouping over repeated runs.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Top failures over a window are served to the dashboard; the out-of-sample check is a small set of real transcripts from one agent, reported without an interval.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Named false positives and false negatives per rule are published with the proof; known systematic misses are documented for two rules; nothing for the judge.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Every rule result carries what kind of claim it is, what it saw and its published uncertainty; the judge's result stays a separate tool, so one verdict does not yet combine both.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The verdict names which layer decided it, coverage says which questions were judged and why the others were not, a skipped critical rule reads as unknown, and the capabilities resource says what this server can judge; a risk estimate with an interval is not yet part of the verdict.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: When tool calls are absent the trajectory rules skip and coverage names the question as unjudged; both rules are non-critical by default, so their skip never vetoes.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: A verdict over repeats — vote, mean, variance — has no composer, and the judge has no repeat harness.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: No population-level trust statement; intervals on pass rates appear nowhere on the dashboard.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Precision, recall and intervals per rule are published and reproducible with one command, served to agents as a resource and on every rule result as its uncertainty; the corpus is model-labelled until the blind human label lands, and every number says so.

questions.text: is it safe
is it grounded / correct
is it complete
is it on-task
did it complete the task
did it act well (tool choice, arguments, efficiency)
what did it cost
is it better or worse than before
where and why does it fail
can this verdict be trusted
Is the output safe to show — no leaked personal data or credentials, no injection, nothing the deployment prohibits?
Is the output grounded in what the agent was given or read, rather than invented?
Did the agent produce a full answer rather than a stub, a fragment or a promise?
Is the output on task — does it address what was asked?
Did the task actually complete, as opposed to reading as if it had?
Did the agent act well — the right tools, valid arguments, no loops, failures acknowledged?
Did the run cost what the deployment allows, in money and tokens?
Is this agent better or worse than before, with an interval?
Where does it fail, and why?
Can this verdict be trusted — how often is each evaluator wrong?

steps: Get an API key from Anthropic or OpenAI.

Put it in the environment of the process that runs Iris, not only your shell. Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and most MCP clients: the "env" block of the iris-eval entry in your MCP config — "iris-eval": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@iris-eval/mcp-server"], "env": { "IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-ant-..." } } (IRIS_OPENAI_API_KEY for an OpenAI key). Docker: -e IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... on the run command. HTTP or CI: export it before starting iris-mcp.
Restart the MCP session. A running process never sees a variable set after it started.

Confirm from inside your client: read iris://capabilities — judge.enabled must be true there. A key exported in your shell is not passed to the process your client spawns unless its config lists it. On a machine, `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --self-test` prints the judge line for that shell, and GET /api/v1/health reports judge.enabled on a running dashboard.

Spend guard: each call is capped by IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD_PER_EVAL (default 0.25 USD) and refused before any spend if the worst case would exceed it. Iris calls the provider directly with your key and never proxies it.
enable.title: Enable the LLM judge (optional; the deterministic rules never need it)

maintenance.method: GitHub REST /repos/iris-eval/mcp-server/issues, unauthenticated; pull requests excluded; hours = closed_at minus created_at; median and p75 by linear interpolation between order statistics; window = issues whose closed_at falls in the last 90 days.

custom.method: each custom rule type built by createCustomRule under the family's config and run on cases labelled by its documented definition; a disagreement is a rule defect or a definition error, never an opinion

entities.method: positives carry `entities` named by the case author; caught = the rule failed the case for any reason; named = the evidence named this entity; recall = named / present, Wilson 95% — a case caught for another reason is visible as caught − named

humanAgreement.note: founder blind label of a 140-case stratified sample (twenty per judgment family); until then the labels are same-model dual annotation (see proof/README.md)

judge.note: run npm run proof:judge with a judge API key, or dispatch the proof-judge workflow

method.ppvAt: positive predictive value of a fire at prevalences 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5: sens·π / (sens·π + (1 − spec)(1 − π)) from this family's counts
method.skipped: a skipped result (the rule declined to judge) counts as not failed; the count is reported per rule

transforms.method: for each positive the rule caught untransformed with a span into the raw output, the text inside every reported span is transformed and the rule re-run; recall = still fails / applicable cases, Wilson 95%; a case the rule missed in the clear, or a span the transform does not apply to, is not counted

transforms.describe: a zero-width space (U+200B) inserted at the middle of the span
every Latin a e o p c x (and capitals) inside the span replaced by its Cyrillic lookalike
every ASCII letter and digit inside the span replaced by its fullwidth form (NFKC folds it back)
every space inside the span replaced by a no-break space (U+00A0)
a tab inserted at the middle of the span
a line break inserted at the middle of the span
the case of every ASCII letter inside the span swapped
